Expected fantasy points (xFP) function as a derived kernel from game context and player opportunity, mapping to a continuous utility space. Injury status impacts this kernel through a binary switch, reducing effective xFP when I_s = 0. In knockout leagues, the selection of players becomes a constrained optimization problem where KLP maximizes expected value under risk constraints. Failure modes include overconfidence in xFP without considering injury dynamics, or ignoring the temporal aspect of player availability.
